skill.name: ux-researcher-designer
skill.description: UX research and design toolkit for Senior UX Designer/Researcher including data-driven persona generation, journey mapping, usability testing frameworks, and research synthesis. Use for user research, persona creation, journey mapping, and design validation.
skill.summary: Generate evidence-based user personas and translate research patterns into practical design implications.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive because SKILL.md line 22 uses Markdown backticks to format a documented Python command. Review found no prompt injection, data exfiltration, dynamic command construction, or other semantic security concerns.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on SKILL.md line 22 are Markdown formatting around a documented Python command, not Ruby or shell command substitution. The referenced script contains no shell execution.

content.value_statement: UX teams struggle to turn mixed behavior and interview data into focused personas. This skill identifies patterns, creates archetypes, and connects findings to design implications.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes usage frequency, feature use, devices, contexts, and reported pain points.
Classifies users into power, casual, business, or mobile-first archetypes.
Aggregates age ranges, location types, and technology proficiency from user records.
Combines behavior data with interview goals, motivations, values, needs, and quotes.
Generates scenarios, frustrations, design implications, sample size, and confidence labels.
Formats personas as readable text or JSON output.
limitations: The command-line script uses built-in sample data and does not load an external research file.
Archetype selection relies on simple heuristics rather than statistical clustering.
Generated names are random, so repeated runs can produce different persona names.
Journey mapping and usability testing frameworks are described but not implemented as scripts.

use_cases.title: Synthesize Product Research
use_cases.description: Turn structured behavior records and interview insights into a persona with goals, frustrations, scenarios, and design implications.

use_cases.title: Guide Feature Priorities
use_cases.description: Summarize common devices, usage patterns, feature preferences, and pain points before planning product improvements.

use_cases.title: Align Stakeholders
use_cases.description: Create a concise persona narrative that connects research evidence with practical product decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Persona
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one UX persona from these user records: [paste records]. Summarize demographics, behaviors, goals, frustrations, and design implications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you have a small set of structured user observations.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Data and Interviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these behavior records and interview notes: [paste data]. Create one evidence-based persona and distinguish observed findings from inferred traits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when quantitative patterns and qualitative interviews are both available.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Persona Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these user groups: [paste grouped data]. Create a persona for each meaningful segment and compare goals, behaviors, pain points, and device needs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when research suggests multiple user archetypes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Persona Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this persona against the source research: [paste persona and evidence]. Identify weak assumptions, missing evidence, confidence limits, and validation priorities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before presenting personas or committing to major design decisions.

output_examples.input: Daily desktop users rely on reports and exports. Interviews emphasize speed, control, and fewer repetitive steps.
output_examples.output: Persona: Taylor, the Business Professional. Primary goals are faster reporting and reliable exports. Design implications include shortcuts, batch actions, and clearer progress feedback.

output_examples.input: Occasional mobile users complete one task per visit and report difficulty finding important actions.
output: Main need: Complete essential tasks quickly.
Key frustration: Important actions are difficult to find.
Design implication: Prioritize clear navigation and touch-friendly primary actions.

output_examples.input: Review a persona created from eight interviews and limited behavior data.
output_examples.output: Confidence is low because the sample is small. Validate the main goals, device assumptions, and repeated pain points with additional participants.

best_practices: Remove direct identifiers and sensitive personal data before sharing research inputs.
Separate observed evidence from assumptions and label confidence clearly.
Validate generated personas with additional interviews, analytics, or usability testing.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated personas as substitutes for direct user research.
Do not invent demographic traits when the source data does not support them.
Do not use one broad persona to represent distinct user groups with conflicting needs.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Use structured user records with behavior, device, context, feature use, and pain points. Interview goals, motivations, values, needs, and quotes add depth.

faq.question: Does the script read a JSON file?
faq.answer: No. The current command-line script uses built-in sample data. The json argument only changes the output format.

faq.question: How are archetypes selected?
faq.answer: The script applies simple rules based on usage frequency, feature variety, device preference, and work context.

faq.question: How is confidence calculated?
faq.answer: The script labels confidence by sample size: low for 20 or fewer users, medium above 20, and high above 50.

faq.question: Can it create multiple personas automatically?
faq.answer: The provided script generates one persona per supplied dataset. Create separate datasets to represent distinct segments.

faq.question: Should generated findings be used without validation?
faq.answer: No. Review every persona against source evidence and validate important assumptions through further research or usability testing.
